title: Neural Bass Drop: Soft-Body Sound Resonance
description: A BoomBox emits visible sound waves that deform a soft-body BrainStem model floating nearby. The user clicks the BoomBox to trigger bass pulses, adjusts frequency with a slider, and drags the BrainStem to reposition it relative to the speaker. Closer proximity causes more dramatic jelly-like deformations on the brain mesh.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 (via importmap from cdn.jsdelivr.net) that implements a soft-body sound resonance simulation. Load BoomBox.glb and BrainStem.glb using GLTFLoader. Scene setup: Place the BoomBox on the left side of the scene at (-2, 0, 0) scaled to be roughly 1.5 units tall. Place the BrainStem on the right at (2, 0.5, 0) scaled similarly. Use a PerspectiveCamera at (0, 2, 6) looking at the origin. Add ambient light (intensity 0.4), a warm point light near the BoomBox (orange, intensity 2), and a cool directional light from above. Use a dark background color (#1a1a2e). Soft-body simulation: After loading the BrainStem, traverse its meshes and store original vertex positions. Each frame, apply a sine-wave vertex displacement to simulate jelly-like wobble. The displacement amplitude should scale inversely with the distance between the BoomBox and BrainStem positions, so closer means more wobble. Use a time-based sine function with configurable frequency. Interactions (5 steps): 1) Click the BoomBox to emit a bass pulse, visualized as expanding transparent torus rings (3-4 rings that scale up and fade out from the BoomBox). 2) Each pulse triggers a stronger momentary deformation spike on the BrainStem vertices. 3) Add an HTML range slider for frequency (1-10 Hz) that changes the sine wave speed of the vertex displacement. 4) Implement raycaster-based drag on the BrainStem so the user can reposition it along the XZ plane, changing its distance from the BoomBox. 5) Add a subtle glow post-effect: when deformation amplitude exceeds a threshold, tint the BrainStem material emissive color to pulse red. Use OrbitControls for camera. Ensure vertex normals are recomputed each frame with computeVertexNormals(). Add a small HTML overlay showing the current distance value between the two models.
